text:
sofia: Heads-up — a Dedicated tenant reported repeated 429s this morning even though they show 1000 rps reserved. logs attached, looks like burst credits dropped to 0 then stayed there. any idea why reserved isn't preventing throttles?

matt: did we apply tenant isolation limit before reserved pool accounting? that would cause early 429s if isolation is lower than reserved.

sofia: exact suspicion. stack trace shows request routed to a slab with tenant_isolation_limit=200 and reserved=1000. seems routing chose a constrained node.

anne: that shouldn't happen. the routing policy should prefer nodes that can honor reserved throughput. maybe we changed hint routing when capacity is fragmented.

kai: pinging routing logic owner — we recently added soft-ejection of noisy tenants. could be the eviction marker caused fallback to smaller slab. infra-bot can you show route decision for ts=1712345301?

infra-bot: route-decision for req 1712345301 -> candidate_nodes [node-a(slab=200), node-b(slab=1200)], chosen=node-a, reason=latency_score(+0.2) due to node-b high inflight.

matt: ah — latency_score beat capacity_score. we weight latency higher to meet SLOs, but that ignores reserved guarantees. bug.

sofia: proposal: when key has reserved throughput, add hard bias in candidate scoring to only consider nodes with capacity >= reserved and tenant_isolation_limit >= reserved_threshold. fallback to current policy only if no such node exists.

anne: makes sense. also we need to expose burst credit accounting in console so tenants can see when they dip to 0. right now console shows only "utilization" and not the credit bank.

kai: on enforcement side, we debate per-org vs per-key: reserved is per-org but most traffic is per-key. if we enforce per-key, reserved could be split weirdly. we need clear rule: reserved applies to org-level baseline; keys can consume but burst draws from org-level credit.

matt: agree. keep reserved at org-level for simplicity; per-key rate-limits remain secondary. also implement a soft-smoothing window when credits are depleted to avoid hammer 429 bursts. e.g. allow short refill for inflight requests that started before depletion.

sofia: technical ask: can eng-runtime add a telemetry counter that emits these metrics per-org per-minute: reserved_allowed, used_reserved, burst_drawn, isolation_rejected? we can then build console widgets and alerts.

kai: I can add a metric name proposal: redwood.dedicated.reserved.{org}.allowed | .used | .burst_drawn | .isolation_blocked. Tag by slab_id and region.

anne: UX side — console should show credit timeline + reason codes (routing fallback, isolation block, node_saturation) and a "what to do" panel (increase reservation, change region, contact support).

matt: implementation plan: short term fix: change routing score to respect reserved guarantees (hotfix), add telemetry counters (2 days), console surface (2 sprints).

sofia: sounds good. can someone pick up the routing hotfix today? it's causing customer impact.

kai: i'll take hotfix. will push a config toggle to staging and we can run a canary.

matt: please add unit tests for candidate scoring and an integration test that simulates a reserved tenant hitting shredded slabs.

sofia: thanks — also file a customer incident note. I'll notify support and update the tenant. :thumbsup:
